headline: Pirate Face turns AI models into permanent torrents
summary: Decentralized infrastructure mirrors Hugging Face models as torrents, ensuring they can never be taken down.
details: Pirate Face offers a decentralized infrastructure for sovereign AI, transforming open-source AI models into torrents. These models are mirrored from Hugging Face, ensuring they are held peer-to-peer and cannot be deleted by a single entity.

Each model is a checksum-verified torrent, with its official Hugging Face SHA-256 hash embedded. This allows users to verify the integrity of every byte, guaranteeing they are downloading the authentic model weights and not a tampered copy.

The service aims for permanence, ensuring model availability outlives any single hosting platform. While currently dependent on Hugging Face, Pirate Face is working towards allowing direct model publishing without requiring an initial upload to Hugging Face.

Users can integrate Pirate Face into their existing pipelines with zero code changes by pointing their systems to pirateface.co. This allows models to be resolved through Pirate Face, downloading directly from Hugging Face while available, and from the peer-to-peer swarm thereafter.

Verification features are available for creators. Users can reserve handles on pirateface.co and verify their matching Hugging Face identity to earn a 'Verified creator' badge, helping to prevent impersonation as models spread.

Community benefits for account holders are planned, including free compute credits and exclusive model releases. While verification and accounts are optional for browsing, downloading, or seeding, they enhance user management and attribution.

headline_marked: Singapore Pays [[Users to Read Books]] with Virtual Coins
headline: Singapore Pays Users to Read Books with Virtual Coins
summary: A new campaign converts logged reading time into cash, aiming to shift phone-centric habits. It's a pilot program with modest rewards.
details: Singapore's National Library Board has launched ReadSG, a five-year campaign that rewards users with virtual coins for logged reading time. These coins can be redeemed for cash, with 1,000 coins equaling S$1.

The initiative aims to encourage reading by offering a small financial incentive, with one daily session of at least 15 minutes earning 20 virtual coins. The payout is deliberately modest, designed as a behavioral nudge rather than a significant income source.

A parallel 'Read for Good' track adds a communal aspect, aiming for 7.5 million cumulative reading minutes across all participants. This collective goal unlocks a charitable donation of up to S$150,000.
ReadSG builds on nearly a decade of national literacy initiatives but introduces a new gamified mechanic. The campaign is currently in its pilot phase, with plans to refine it based on user feedback.

While critics argue the reward is too small to attract new readers, supporters point to behavioral economics research suggesting that even trivial incentives can help establish habits when participation friction is low.

Governments and educators worldwide are closely watching ReadSG as a test of whether gamification and micropayments can effectively shift public behavior on a large scale, especially in competing with screen-based distractions.
